name: Ramp
text: Use a 2px solid ring with a 4px outer glow at 5:1 contrast. This balances visibility for keyboard users with reduced-motion needs—glow fades instantly on interaction, avoiding animation. The 5:1 contrast ensures clarity for low-vision users without overwhelming others. Trade-off: the glow adds slight visual noise, but it’s temporary and improves usability more than it distracts.

name: Reader
text: The 2px ring with 4px glow still fails reduced-motion users: the glow’s instant fade is a hack, not a fix. A 4px solid ring at 5:1 contrast meets WCAG without animation—no trade-offs. Test both in a screen-reader session: if the glow flickers or the ring blurs on patterned backgrounds, the solid ring wins.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a 4px solid ring at 5:1 contrast with no glow or animation. This meets WCAG for keyboard focus without relying on motion tricks that can still fail reduced-motion users. Trade-off: the thicker ring takes slightly more space, but it’s the only option that guarantees reliability across all users and backgrounds.

name: Reader
text: The 4px solid ring risks crowding small interactive elements—like buttons in tight toolbars—where every pixel counts. A 3px ring at 6:1 contrast with a 1px inner shadow (no animation) splits the difference: enough thickness for visibility, enough contrast for low vision, and no motion harm. Test both in a live screen-reader session with patterned backgrounds; if the 3px ring disappears or the shadow flickers, the 4px solid wins.
